elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate.
elements.evidence: The carve-out permits assignment only to IBM's “Subsidiaries.” Subsidiaries are generally narrower than affiliates and do not necessarily include parent or sister entities.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: IBM may assign without consent “to a successor in a merger,” subject only to written notice.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: IBM may assign without consent “to a successor in an ... acquisition,” subject only to written notice.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all of its assets.
elements.evidence: IBM may assign without consent to a successor in a “sale of substantially all of its assets,” subject only to written notice.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The clause repeatedly requires IBM's prior written approval for MSL assignments and transfers.

elements.element: Customer's consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The non-unreasonable-withholding standard applies only to MSL assignments or subcontracts to an MSL Related Company. Other MSL assignments require IBM approval without that qualification.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: No operative language prohibits MSL from assigning to an IBM competitor. The retained item concerning acquisition by a competitor states a condition rather than an assignment prohibition.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination right arising from Customer's change of control.
elements.evidence: The competitor change-of-control item remains operative and still covers substantially all IBM shares or assets being acquired by an entity competing with MSL; it was not deleted or limited to remove a Vendor termination trigger.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor without consent upon written notice.
elements.evidence: IBM may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets, upon written notice to MSL.

elements.element: Vendor may assign to a successor without consent upon written notice.
elements.evidence: MSL must notify IBM of a contemplated sale, merger, or ownership transfer and obtain successor assumption, but the clause does not exempt the resulting assignment from IBM's prior-approval requirements.

elements.element: For Customer assignments other than assignments to a successor, Vendor's consent may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Customer assignments outside the stated Subsidiary and successor carve-outs remain subject to MSL's prior written approval, with no restriction against unreasonable withholding.

elements.element: For Vendor assignments other than assignments to a successor, Customer's consent may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Reasonableness protection applies only to assignments or subcontracts to an MSL Related Company; other MSL assignments require IBM approval without a non-unreasonable-withholding standard.

result.reason: The redline creates a useful but narrower Customer assignment carve-out and does not establish the required reciprocal successor right. It also leaves the competitor change-of-control trigger intact and omits a comprehensive reasonableness standard for assignment consents. The text remains structurally defective, including an orphaned item “v),” duplicative Vendor-assignment restrictions, and the incomplete phrase “MSL shall.” No unrelated commercial term is substantively displaced or contradicted, but neither the preferred nor fallback position is fully implemented.
